paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. The believers shared everything, and it started in the heart, because the text says they were "one in heart and soul" (Acts 4:32). Barnabas, whose name means Son of Encouragement, sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet (Acts 4:36-37). Giving was never the hard part to understand, because what matters is that it was real.

Now look at Ananias and Sapphira, because Peter asks, "Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal?" (Acts 5:4). Nobody made them give it all, so they could have kept every bit. Their trouble was pretending to give it all, and Peter says, "You have not lied to men, but to God!" (Acts 5:4). I don't think this is about how much we put in the box, baker, but about whether what we show matches what's in our heart.

This one is heavy, and I think it hurts to read, so I'm not going to dress it up. Great fear came over the whole church (Acts 5:11), and that tells me God takes honesty with Him seriously, and so should I. The good news is that you don't have to fake anything with Him. Bring Him the real offering, even a small one, and bring it with a real heart.
